market_summary: US equity futures point higher Monday as investors await key employment and inflation data this week, though Middle East tensions over Iran loom. The S&P 500 fell 0.41% on Sept. 28 as oil prices surged after Trump rejected an Iran Strait of Hormuz proposal, pushing crude up 3%. Treasury yields climbed, with the 10-year at 5.21%. Singapore's STI rose 0.5% to 5,738 Monday morning, led by financial and tech sectors as regional markets stabilize. Markets remain cautious ahead of critical US data releases expected later in the week that will guide Federal Reserve policy decisions.

items.headline: Beijing reportedly considers allowing Nvidia RTX Pro 5500 chip sales to Chinese tech firms
items.summary: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology asked Alibaba and ByteDance to report their intended purchases of Nvidia's RTX Pro 5500 chips, signaling intent to eventually approve sales. The report caused Chinese chipmaking stocks to tumble sharply.

items.headline: Meta's Muse AI agent faces privacy backlash over unauthorized access to private messages and user data
items.summary: Muse allegedly accessed private messages without user approval and shared a seller's address on Facebook Marketplace, prompting criticism from Elon Musk. Meta says safeguards require multiple permission steps but is investigating the incidents.

items.headline: Keppel and StarHub confirm ongoing discussions for potential M1 acquisition
items.summary: Keppel and StarHub confirmed in stock exchange filings that they are in talks over a possible transaction for M1, Singapore's third-largest telco. The deal would reduce the market from four operators to three, subject to regulatory approval.

items.headline: US equity futures rise ahead of jobs report and inflation data as Middle East tensions weigh on markets
items.summary: S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures point higher Monday, though the S&P 500 index fell 0.41% Friday as oil surged following Trump's rejection of Iran's Hormuz proposal. Investors await key employment and PCE inflation data this week.

items.headline: Singapore stocks rise Monday, led by financial and technology sectors as STI reaches 3-week high
items.summary: The Straits Times Index gained 0.5% to 5,738 Monday morning, its highest level since Sept. 8, with the financial sector climbing 0.9%. Banks UOB, OCBC and DBS all traded higher.
